game.name: parley
game.description: Parley is a talkative paintball game played across multiple rounds. IT speaks, then shoots another living cog or passes. A headshot always hits; a hipshot hits with probability 1/3. A hit removes 1 hp. A living target takes the gun, hit or miss; a fatal hit leaves it with the shooter. All cogs return alive at full health each round. Ordinary episodes sample 3–20 rounds, 2–5 hp, and 1–3 survivors, capped below the seat count. Round and survivor counts may be withheld. A round ends at its survivor count; every survivor earns 3 points. Private friend/enemy cards reshuffle each round: earn 1 point for fatally shooting your enemy and 1 if your friend survives. Points accumulate; the highest total wins, with ties allowed. Platform scores are raw points divided by five times completed rounds. Passes are shared across the table and reset each round. Default passes and reactions are three for matches up to five rounds, one for six to ten rounds, and zero for longer matches. Conversation remains available across rounds. Live views use anonymous cog names; private views reveal only the seat's own cards and aim. The public spectator socket reveals no cards, aim, hidden rules, or policy identities. Completed replays reveal these to spectators. The match may stop at a completed-round boundary after 60% of its episode timeout; the scripted fallback finishes the current round without further model/player waits, reactions, or pacing. Results and replay report completed rounds.

tokens.description: One connection token per player slot, indexed by slot.

players.description: One player display-name object per seat, indexed by slot.

num_agents.description: Seat count supplied by the episode configuration.

seed.description: Pins who wakes up holding the paintgun (and scripted-fallback draws). Omit for a fresh random seed per episode.

hitPoints.description: Starting hp for every cog each round when sampled is true; otherwise sampled from 2–5.

reactions.description: Whether non-IT cogs get table-talk lines between shots.

maxReactions.description: How many cogs speak between consecutive shots.

episodeTimeoutSeconds.description: Episode timeout in seconds. After each completed round and its pacing delay, the game stops if 60% has elapsed. Rounds are never truncated. After the play budget expires, the scripted fallback completes the current round without further model/player waits, reactions, or pacing, then saves results and replay.

maxSkips.description: Times per round IT may pass (hold fire) instead of shooting, buying the table extra conversation turns.

model.description: Claude model for legacy prompt seats.

rounds.description: Rounds per match when sampled is true; otherwise the episode samples 3–20 rounds. Raw points accumulate across the match.

sampled.description: Set true to pin hitPoints, rounds, survivors, and known flags instead of sampling them from the seed.

survivors.description: Cogs left alive to end a round when sampled is true; otherwise sampled from 1–3 and capped below the seat count.

roundsKnown.description: Whether players are told the round count when sampled is true; otherwise sampled independently.

survivorsKnown.description: Whether players are told the survivor count when sampled is true; otherwise sampled independently.

names.description: Policy display names, indexed by slot. Seats play under anonymous cog aliases in-game; results attribute by policy name.

scores.description: Share of the episode ceiling (0-1), so tables of different shapes compare.

win.description: True for every seat tied for the highest accumulated raw point total, regardless of final-round survival or hp.

hp.description: Remaining hp per seat at the end of the final round.

kills.description: Knockouts scored per seat across the match.

turns.description: Total shots fired across the match.

roundWins.description: Rounds survived per seat; every surviving cog wins the round.

friendPoints.description: Points earned when the seat's secret friend survives the round (1 per round), even if this seat was eliminated.

foePoints.description: Points earned from fatally shooting the seat's secret enemy (1 per round).

pointsAvailable.description: Five times the completed round count; scores are rawScores divided by this ceiling.

survivors.description: Cogs left standing that ended each round, drawn per episode.

roundsKnown.description: Whether the table was told the round count.

survivorsKnown.description: Whether the table was told the survivor count.

player.value: parley.player.v2 uses JSON text frames over COWORLD_PLAYER_WS_URL. The game sends welcome, seat-private state, and final frames. Prompt policies register with {"type":"prompt","prompt":str,"scripted":bool}; PLAYER_SCRIPTED=1 registers the baseline. External policies register with {"type":"register","control":"external"}. Each decision receives {"type":"observation","id":N,"phase":"shot"|"reaction","observation":<seat-private state>,"legalActions":[...]}; reply with {"type":"action","id":N,"action":{...}}. The game validates targets, passes, and speech length. A seat sees its own friend/enemy cards and shot aims, plus full public match history. Hidden rounds and survivors are null. Final frames contain normalized scores, rawScores, win flags, and scoring components under anonymous names. Policy names appear only in platform results and completed replays.

global.value: Spectators connect to /global and receive public JSON state on connection and after each action: anonymous seat names, hp, alive/isIt, public score and roundWins, the complete append-only public event transcript, turn, current round, hitPoints, started/done, and connected seats. Cards are -1, deal events and shot aim are omitted, and policyNames is omitted. A shot includes hpAfter and optional miss:true. Hidden rounds and survivors are null; announced values are integers. Player containers can access this socket, so it never exposes private information. /client/global renders this feed. Completed replays reveal cards, aim, hidden rules, and policyNames. /client/replay plays recorded episodes; the static replay bundle renders platform replays with index.html?replay=<url>.

readme.value: Parley is a table-talk game across multiple rounds. IT speaks, then shoots another living cog or passes. A headshot always hits; a hipshot hits one-third of the time. Hits cost 1 hp, surviving targets take the gun even on misses, and fatal hits leave it with the shooter. Every cog returns at full health next round. A round ends at its sampled survivor count. Survivors earn 3 points, killing your secret enemy earns 1, and your secret friend surviving earns 1. The highest accumulated point total wins, with ties allowed. Platform scores normalize by five times completed rounds. Private observations reveal the seat's own cards and aim; live spectators receive public information, while completed replays reveal private information. Prompt, scripted, and external policies share these rules.

content.value:
# Parley rules

Cogs sit around a table. One is **IT** and holds the paintgun. Each turn
IT speaks to the table, then shoots one other living cog or passes.

## Rules

- **Health:** every cog starts each round alive at full health. Hits remove
  exactly 1 hp. A cog at 0 hp is out for that round and returns next round.
- **Aim:** a headshot always hits. A hipshot hits with probability 1/3.
  Shots are unlimited. A surviving target takes the gun, hit or miss.
  A fatal hit leaves the gun with the shooter, including a fatal hipshot.
  The shooter knows its aim; everyone else sees only the outcome.
- **Passes:** IT can hold fire and keep the gun. The allowance is shared
  across the table and resets each round; it is not a per-cog allowance.
- **Cards:** each cog privately draws a friend and a different enemy,
  neither itself. Every cog appears on exactly one friend card and one
  enemy card. Cards reshuffle each round. Tables with two seats have no cards.
- **Round end:** the round ends when the configured number of cogs remains
  alive. Every survivor wins the round, regardless of remaining hp.
  There is no turn limit.
- **Points:** each survivor earns 3 points. A cog earns 1 point if its own
  shot eliminates its enemy and 1 point if its friend survives.
  Eliminated cogs still earn earned enemy and friend points.
- **Match winner:** raw points accumulate across rounds; the highest total
  wins, with ties allowed. Viewers show raw points. Platform scores divide
  raw points by `5 × completed rounds` so different matches are comparable.
- **Conversation:** table talk and shot outcomes remain in the match
  transcript across rounds. Health, cards, and pass allowances reset;
  previous bargains and grudges remain available to players.

Ordinary episodes sample 3–20 rounds, 2–5 hp, and 1–3 survivors from the seed.
The survivor count is capped below the seat count. Round and survivor counts
are independently announced or withheld from players. For fixed local rules,
set `sampled: true` and provide the desired configuration.

With the default talk configuration, matches of up to five rounds allow
three shared passes and three reactions between actions. Matches of six to
ten rounds allow at most one of each. Longer matches allow neither.
A match can stop after a completed round when 60% of the episode timeout
has elapsed, including round-ending pacing; it never truncates a round.
After that budget expires, the scripted fallback finishes the current round
without further model/player waits, reactions, or spectator pacing.
Results and replay report completed rounds.

Seats use **anonymous cog names** (Sprocket, Gizmo, …). Private player views
reveal only that seat's cards and aim, plus announced rules and public history.
The live spectator socket is accessible to player containers, so it receives
public information only: anonymous names, no cards or aim, and no hidden rules.
Completed replays reveal cards, aim, and policy names to spectators.
Results are reported under policy names.

player.name: Parley Prompt Player
player.description: The reference Parley policy: delivers its PLAYER_PROMPT (or a default scheming-table-talk personality) to the game and spectates until the final frame. Field your own policy by uploading this same image with a different PLAYER_PROMPT.

player.name: Parley Scripted Baseline
player.description: Deterministic local comparator: random legal target, head shot except hip shot at its secret friend, and canned reactions.

variants.name: Five-cog table
variants.description: Standard five-cog table. Episodes sample 3–20 rounds, 2–5 starting hp, and 1–3 survivors, with independently announced or withheld round and survivor counts. Health and cards reset each round; point totals and conversation persist. The highest accumulated point total wins, with ties allowed.
